source_text: Denique ut intellegas, non eum naturae eorum exprobrare, sed vitae; sequitur: Scio quia filii Abrahae estis [n205] . Ecce de qua illi se liberos dixerant originis dignitate; nunc cui servituti obnoxii sint demonstrat, dicens: Quaeritis me interficere, quia sermo meus non capit in vobis. Ego quod audivi apud Patrem meum, loquor; et vos quae vidistis apud patrem vestrum, facitis [n206] .
pass_a_gloss: Finally that you may understand, that he is not reproaching their nature, but their life; it follows: I know that you are sons of Abraham. See about which dignity of origin those had said they were free; now he demonstrates to which slavery they are liable, saying: You seek to kill me, because my speech does not take in you. I speak what I have heard with my Father; and you do what you have seen with your father.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: To make you understand that he reproaches their lives rather than their nature, he continues: “I know that you are Abraham's children” (John 8:37). There is the dignity of descent on account of which they had declared themselves free. Now he shows the slavery to which they are subject: “You seek to kill me, because my word finds no room in you. I speak what I have heard with my Father; and you do what you have seen with your father” (John 8:37–38).

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.
